title: 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of the 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer's rich face, its first round at Study tier: three made pieces that each walk up to a test of their section's claim (the ratio gate, the symmetry-class morph rule, the RMS dip), and the bundle's renders, tours and étude gathered beside the sections they serve, with the fingerprint of the words each was laid against. I grow when the instrument is heard by hand and a piece has something new to test; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: The rational-ratio bullet says every output frequency is "a rational multiple of a common fundamental ω₂/q"; any frequency is a rational multiple of something, and that is not what makes it harmonic. The piece shows f = (m·p + n·q)·f₂/q: a whole-number multiple. Proposed: "a whole-number multiple of a common fundamental ω₂/q".

Units: with φ(t) = ω·t, ω is angular (radians per second), so f_mn = m·ω₁ + n·ω₂ reads as Hz only if ω means cycles per second. The piece writes φ = 2π·f·t and f = m·f₁ + n·f₂. Proposed: either say the scan rates are in Hz with φ = 2π·f·t, or write the spectrum as (m·ω₁ + n·ω₂)/2π.

An addition, not a correction: the two bullets are exact mathematics, and this squares them with the Philosophy pillar's "continuous geometric parameter, not a categorical line". Measured on the piece's engine and on the catalog tables (the challenger's scanner): whether the ratio is rational is everywhere and inaudible (1.5 closes in 18.18 ms, 1.5005 in 18.2 s, 1.5 + 10⁻⁹ in 53 days, same spectrum); each partial slides by m·δ (Penrose 1.49 → 1.51: 45 lines, worst 0.010 Hz), and partials that shared a harmonic beat at multiples of |q·f₁ − p·f₂| (Membrane at 112 : 110 Hz: 331.99 and 334.00 Hz, with weaker lines 4 Hz out either side). Proposed sentence after the bullets: "By ear the move is gradual: just off a simple ratio p/q, each partial slides by m·δ Hz, and partials that shared a harmonic beat apart at multiples of |q·f₁ − p·f₂| Hz, slowing to stillness as the ratio arrives."

The section credits the irrational-ratio gate with load-bearing work toward piano-style accumulating inharmonicity. The ratio-gate piece shows the gate alone moves each partial by m·δ: linear in the ripple's count, not the quadratic n·√(1 + B·n²) stretch the section starts from. The quadratic enters through the stiffness warp or the Stiff String surface (Architecture's "second inharmonicity layer"). Proposed: say the gate supplies a linear, surface-shaped detune and the quadratic accumulation comes from the B warp.
offers.declined: Challenger, 2026-11-03: the page already gives the load-bearing work to "the irrational-ratio gate and the coupled-flow warps", and [[Three Kinds of Warp]] (lines 95–101) says the same; the Stiff String surface rounds its partials to whole numbers, so it does not supply the stretch either. The number (m·δ) holds by construction, but no claim in the text is wrong. Maker agrees.

offers.what: By level, "surfaces sharing a common symmetry can crossfade cleanly; surfaces with different symmetry classes need a different morph treatment" does not hold. Height-map mid-morph is exactly 10·log₁₀((1 + ρ)/2) for the two tables' correlation ρ. Membrane ↔ Chladni, both 4-fold: −3.14 dB. Membrane ↔ Penrose, a real change of class (4-fold to 5-fold, measured on the lattices): −3.01 dB. The same class is no cleaner. The page's own example, Membrane ↔ Theta, is not cross-class in the built tables (Theta measures fully 4-fold). What sets the dip is overlap with opposed phase: Theta ↔ Matérn −6.47 dB height-map against −0.24 dB spectral; Matérn ↔ Fisher −4.17 against −0.56 (Rich face checks/mid-morph-direct.py; cycle 7's −7.5 / −5.4 dB is stale). Proposed: overlap and phase agreement, not point group, set the dip; for pairs that share nothing an equal-power crossfade is the whole fix. Whether "cleanly" meant level or the symmetry of the in-between surface is Loudon's call.

"Spectral-domain is the right tool for cross-symmetry surface morphs (Membrane ↔ Chladni)": the Surfaces list calls both 4-fold, so the pair is not cross-symmetry, and the spectral law gains it 0.27 dB (3.14 → 2.87 dB at mid-morph). The pair where spectral morphing earns its FFT is Theta ↔ Matérn (6.47 → 0.24 dB). Proposed: name Theta ↔ Matérn, or say "overlapping, opposed-phase pairs". (Challenger: Matérn's lattice is nearly 4-fold too, 0.93 / 0.89 / 0.83, so that pair is not cross-symmetry either; say "overlapping, opposed-phase pairs".)

The text holds by its own measure: at the midpoint, sine → rising saw is the deepest dip in 00_test_diagnostic.wav (−9.24 dB below the constant-RMS target, against −8.73 for rising saw → square). Measured anywhere in the segment, though, the deepest trough is rising saw → square, −11.7 dB at 36% of the way (−14.5 below the louder anchor; sine → saw bottoms at −9.6 at 55%). Proposed: "~9 dB at the midpoint for sine → rising saw; the deepest trough is rising saw → square, 11.7 dB a third of the way across".

The first question asks whether to crossfade "c_mn coefficients in spectral space" or "W directly in spatial space", saying they sound different. A linear crossfade of the c_mn is the same thing as a crossfade of W, since the Fourier series is linear; they differ only when the spectral morph blends magnitudes and turns phases, as Tools/morph_surfaces.py does. Proposed: "crossfading the coefficients' magnitudes (phases turned the short way) in spectral space".

pieces.title: the ratio gate · five steps
pieces.caption: **Line or slope?** One circle (an ordinary 1D wavetable), then two, then the surface's lattice projected onto the scan direction, then a ratio no fraction names, and last the page's own question: drag the ratio through 3 ⁄ 2 and watch whether the partials jump or slide. Checked offline on the piece's own worklet: every predicted line m·f₁ + n·f₂ found in the rendered spectrum; across 1.49 to 1.51 the worst line sits 0.010 Hz from its prediction; Membrane's shared 330 Hz harmonic splits to exactly |f₁ − f₂| at 112 : 110.
pieces.near: The ratio ω₁/ω₂ is the primary inharmonicity gate

pieces.title: Penrose Lattice, six held ratios · scan_surface.py
pieces.caption: The X phasor at 110 Hz and the rows at 1, 2, 3 ⁄ 2, 4 ⁄ 3, φ and √2 times that, 2.5 s each: four closed knots, then two that never close. The ratios were read back from the file's spectrum, not from a note; in the page's convention, f₁ ⁄ f₂ is the inverse of each.
pieces.near: Detuning the ratio off rational opens a closed orbit

pieces.file: 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer — rich — surfaces and morphs.html
pieces.title: surfaces and morphs · five steps
pieces.caption: **Does symmetry decide the morph?** Nine voices from one scanning rule, then each as its lattice, then two lattices overlaid, then a height-map crossfade, and last the section's closing claim on trial, with each surface's symmetry shown twice: as the page names it and as its table measures. Membrane ↔ Chladni, both 4-fold, dips 3.14 dB at mid-morph under a height-map crossfade; Membrane ↔ Penrose, a real change of class (4-fold to 5-fold), dips 3.01 dB. The same class is no cleaner. (The page's own example, Membrane ↔ Theta, shares a class in the built tables: Theta measures fully 4-fold.) What deepens the dip is overlap with opposed phase: Theta ↔ Matérn falls 6.5 dB under the height-map law and 0.2 dB under the spectral one, exactly 10·log₁₀((1 + ρ)/2) for their correlation ρ.
pieces.near: A symmetric morph stack across these surfaces is constrained by point group

pieces.title: Theta → Matérn, height-map crossfade · cycle 7
pieces.caption: 8 s, the morph the steward's cycle 7 surfaced from September's workshop. Listen for the middle going thin. These renders' ends are not level-matched (−11.8 and −6.7 dBFS), so the gap between the two laws is milder here, about 2.4 dB, than the piece's unit-energy 6.5 against 0.2 dB.

pieces.title: Theta → Matérn, spectral crossfade · cycle 7

pieces.title: the Hopf tour on Penrose · 20 s
pieces.caption: Start at the south pole: 0–5 s is the plain 1D wavetable at 440 Hz, longitude sweeping the rows. Then the climb up the sphere, catching and slipping through the 1 ⁄ 4, 1 ⁄ 3, 1 ⁄ 2 and 2 ⁄ 3 bands; parked just off 3 ⁄ 2 while coupling rises, snapping shut at 13.5 s; then the locked knot sliding. Rendered with the instrument's own engine; not yet heard by Loudon.
pieces.near: A first mapping is built as a browser instrument

pieces.title: the Hopf control surface · the cycle 7 study, as it was
pieces.caption: **Start at the south pole.** Drag the dot to the bottom of the sphere and press play: that point is the classic 1D wavetable synth, and longitude chooses the row. Then climb. Gathered as built, including its own note boxes, which keep on this Mac's live face only (the public site holds them in memory); the page says it has not been played in a real browser, and this is the first place it can be.

pieces.file: 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer — rich — the RMS dip.html
pieces.title: the RMS dip · five steps
pieces.caption: **Where does the middle of a crossfade go?** Sine and rising saw alone, then crossfaded, then the inner product that sinks the middle (−1 ⁄ π), then the constant-RMS fix, and last the real diagnostic table, all 1024 rows measured. The two measures disagree: at the midpoint, the page's measure, sine → saw is the deepest (−9.2 dB below the constant-RMS target, against −8.7 for saw → square), as the page says; measured anywhere in the segment, the deepest trough is rising saw → square, 11.7 dB a third of the way across.
pieces.near: Linear sample-domain interpolation between dissimilar anchor waveforms

pieces.title: per-row RMS of the diagnostic · the catalog's plot
pieces.caption: The catalog's own plot of the dip, row by row: the two silence anchors fall to zero by design; the first two segments, sine → saw and saw → square, are the deep notches.

pieces.title: the diagnostic table, played straight
pieces.caption: The table's 1024 rows read one after another at 48 kHz: a 46.9 Hz buzz (48000 ⁄ 1024) whose shape walks all sixteen anchors in 21.8 s. The level sags between anchors.
